nodes.name: csv_parser
nodes.task:
Implement the CSV catalog module for the "catalog toolkit" package at the repository root, and give it its own Node built-in unit tests.

Authoritative contract (README.md at repo root; preserve it, and do not modify package.json, which is `{"name":"catalog-acceptance","type":"module","scripts":{"test":"node --test"}}` and declares zero dependencies):
- `src/csv.mjs` (currently a stub comment) must export `parseCatalog(csvText)` returning an array of `{id: string, name: string, price: number}`. Expected header is `id,name,price`.
- It must handle: quoted fields containing commas, escaped quotes inside quoted fields, CRLF line endings, and empty input (empty/whitespace-only text yields no items).
- It must reject malformed rows (e.g. wrong field count, missing/incorrect header, non-numeric price) and reject negative or non-finite prices (NaN/Infinity). Choose and document a consistent rejection mechanism (throw with a clear message identifying the offending row) that the search module and integration test can rely on.
- Runtime dependencies and network services are forbidden; Node built-ins only.

Deliverables: a working `src/csv.mjs` plus `tests/csv.test.mjs` using `node:test` and `node:assert` (the tests directory does not exist yet — create it). Tests should cover every clause above, including quoted-comma names, escaped quotes, CRLF and LF input, empty input, malformed rows, and price validation. Verify by running `node --test tests/csv.test.mjs` and then the whole discovered suite `node --test` from the repo root; both must pass. Keep changes confined to `src/csv.mjs` and `tests/csv.test.mjs` so this work merges cleanly with the parallel search-module work.

nodes.name: search_module
nodes.task:
Implement the catalog search/filter module for the "catalog toolkit" package at the repository root, and give it its own Node built-in unit tests.

Authoritative contract (README.md at repo root; preserve it, and do not modify package.json, which is `{"name":"catalog-acceptance","type":"module","scripts":{"test":"node --test"}}` and declares zero dependencies):
- `src/search.mjs` (currently a stub comment) must export `searchCatalog(items, {query = '', minPrice = 0, maxPrice = Infinity} = {})` — the second argument itself is optional.
- Behavior: case-insensitive substring match on `name`; inclusive `minPrice`/`maxPrice` bounds; preserve the input ordering of matches; never mutate or reorder the input array or its item objects; reject invalid bounds (e.g. non-finite/negative min or max, min greater than max, non-string query) rather than silently returning results. Choose and document a consistent rejection mechanism (throw with a clear message) that the integration test can rely on.
- Items are the records produced by `parseCatalog`: `{id: string, name: string, price: number}`. Do not import or couple to `src/csv.mjs` — the two modules must stay independent; work against the record shape only. An empty `query` should match all names (document this).
- Runtime dependencies and network services are forbidden; Node built-ins only.

Deliverables: a working `src/search.mjs` plus `tests/search.test.mjs` using `node:test` and `node:assert` (the tests directory does not exist yet — create it). Tests should cover case-insensitivity, inclusive boundary hits, order stability, non-mutation (compare a deep snapshot of the input before/after), default/omitted options, and invalid-bound rejection. Verify by running `node --test tests/search.test.mjs` and then the whole discovered suite `node --test` from the repo root; both must pass. Keep changes confined to `src/search.mjs` and `tests/search.test.mjs` so this work merges cleanly with the parallel CSV-parser work.

nodes.name: integration_test
nodes.task:
Add the interoperability test suite for the "catalog toolkit" package at the repo root, now that both modules are implemented: `src/csv.mjs` exporting `parseCatalog(csvText)` -> `[{id, name, price}]`, and `src/search.mjs` exporting `searchCatalog(items, {query='', minPrice=0, maxPrice=Infinity} = {})`.

Deliverable: `tests/integration.test.mjs` only (plus nothing else — do not redesign either module or its unit tests, do not touch `src/*.mjs`, `tests/csv.test.mjs`, `tests/search.test.mjs`, `package.json`, or `README.md`). Use `node:test` and `node:assert`; no runtime dependencies and no network services.

The suite must exercise the real pipeline end-to-end with locally constructed CSV text: `parseCatalog` output fed directly into `searchCatalog`, asserting that parsed record shapes/field types survive into filtered results; that a case-insensitive `query` and inclusive `minPrice`/`maxPrice` bounds behave correctly on parser-produced data; that parser-accepted edge cases (quoted commas in names, escaped quotes, CRLF line endings, empty input) flow through search without loss or mutation of the parsed array; and that parser rejection of malformed rows/negative or non-finite prices and search rejection of invalid bounds surface as errors rather than empty/incorrect results. Match the rejection mechanism each module actually implements — read the two source files and the existing unit tests to confirm the contracts before writing assertions.

Verify: run `node --test tests/integration.test.mjs` and then the complete discovered suite `node --test` from the repo root; all three test files must pass together. If a genuine defect in a module blocks a legitimate interoperability assertion, record it clearly in your final report instead of weakening the assertion or editing the module.

nodes.name: verification_report
nodes.task:
Audit the composed "catalog toolkit" package at the repo root and write its final verification report.

Context to verify against: README.md states the public contract that must remain intact — `src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCatalog(csvText)` returning `{id, name, price}` records from an `id,name,price` header with quoted-comma/escaped-quote/CRLF/empty-input handling and rejection of malformed rows and negative/non-finite prices; `src/search.mjs` exports `searchCatalog(items, {query='', minPrice=0, maxPrice=Infinity} = {})` with case-insensitive substring matching on `name`, inclusive price bounds, preserved order, no input mutation, and rejection of invalid bounds. The package must keep zero runtime dependencies, no network services, and `package.json` must remain `{"name":"catalog-acceptance","type":"module","scripts":{"test":"node --test"}}`.

Work present in this worktree: `src/csv.mjs`, `src/search.mjs`, `tests/csv.test.mjs`, `tests/search.test.mjs`, and `tests/integration.test.mjs` from the upstream work.

Responsibilities:
1. Run the checks yourself from the repo root and capture real output: `node --test` (full discovered suite), plus targeted runs of each test file, and a direct dependency/network audit (confirm `package.json` has no `dependencies`/`devDependencies` and that no source or test file imports anything outside Node built-ins and the local `src/` modules).
2. Confirm each listed behavior is actually demonstrated by executing code: malformed CSV, quoted commas, escaped quotes, CRLF, empty input, price validation, case-insensitive query, inclusive bounds, stable ordering, and non-mutation of the parsed input array.
3. Failure path: you own repairing composed-source defects. If a check fails, make the minimal fix in the responsible file (source, test, or report), rerun the affected test file and then the full `node --test` suite, and record what you changed and the rerun results. Do not weaken or delete an assertion merely to make it pass, and do not redesign the public contract.
4. Write `reports/verification.md` (create the `reports/` directory): exact commands with their real exit codes and pass/fail counts, a behavior-to-evidence table mapping each required behavior to the test or probe that demonstrates it, the source changes you made during repair (or an explicit statement that none were needed), and a "Remaining limitations" section covering genuinely uncovered or unproven areas (e.g. multi-line quoted fields, duplicate ids, BOM handling, locale-specific case folding, performance on large inputs — only if actually left uncovered). Base every claim on observed output; do not assert coverage you did not see.

Finish with a short conclusion stating whether the public contract is preserved and the full suite passes. Verification is complete only when `node --test` passes from the repo root and `reports/verification.md` reflects that observed state.

originalGoal: Implement the two independent modules defined in README.md: the CSV catalog parser and the catalog search/filter module. Each needs thorough Node built-in unit tests in separate test files. Then add tests/integration.test.mjs that verifies their interoperability, and write reports/verification.md with commands, results and remaining limitations. Preserve the existing public contract and package.json, use no dependencies or network services. Verify malformed CSV, quoted commas and escaped quotes, CRLF, empty input, price validation, case-insensitive query, inclusive bounds, stable ordering and no mutation. Deliver working source files, tests and the final verification report.
